title: Inference
tagline: Decoding and sampling, the KV cache, batching, quantisation, speculative decoding and long context
summary: Every generated token costs time, memory and money. This course explains decoding and sampling strategies, the key–value cache, batching and memory management in serving systems, quantisation and distillation, speculative decoding, long-context inference, and how latency, throughput and cost trade off.

overview: LLM inference is the process of generating text token by token. This course covers decoding, caching, speculative decoding, and efficient serving.
The key insight is that inference cost scales with sequence length. KV caching and speculative decoding trade compute for latency.
outcomes: Explain token-by-token inference and the KV cache.
Describe speculative decoding and draft-verify schemes.
Implement efficient batched serving and continuous batching.
Analyze inference latency and memory trade-offs.

history.title: vLLM
history.detail: Kwon et al. introduced PagedAttention and vLLM for efficient LLM serving.

history.title: Speculative decoding
history.detail: Leviathan et al. showed draft models can speed up decoding without changing output distribution.

history.title: Continuous batching
history.detail: Anyscale introduced continuous batching for dynamic request scheduling.

references.title: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention
Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding

chapters.title: Decoding and sampling
chapters.summary: Greedy decoding, temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling, and repetition penalties.

chapters.title: The key–value cache
chapters.summary: Incremental decoding, the memory of the cache, and multi-query and grouped-query attention at inference time.

chapters.title: Batching and serving systems
chapters.summary: Continuous batching, paged attention, prefill and decode phases, and serving frameworks.

chapters.title: Quantisation
chapters.summary: Integer and low-bit formats, post-training quantisation methods such as GPTQ and AWQ, and quantised caches.

chapters.title: Distillation and pruning
chapters.summary: Smaller models through distillation and structured and unstructured pruning.

chapters.title: Speculative decoding
chapters.summary: Draft models, verification and parallel decoding schemes.

chapters.title: Long-context inference
chapters.summary: Extending the context window, position interpolation, retrieving distant information and attention sinks.

chapters.title: Latency, throughput and cost
chapters.summary: Measuring and optimising time to first token, tokens per second and cost per token.
